drivingQuestion: Why must the mishna teach that betrothal after halitza is ineffective?

segments.he: בֵּין יָבָם אֶחָד לִשְׁתֵּי יְבָמוֹת כּוּ׳. בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, דְּאָמַר כּוּלֵּהּ בֵּיתָא בְּלָאו קָאֵי — אִיצְטְרִיךְ לְאַשְׁמוֹעִינַן דְּאֵין קִדּוּשִׁין תּוֹפְסִין בְּחַיָּיבֵי לָאוִין.
segments.en: § It was taught in the mishna: Nothing is effective after ḥalitza, «both» in cases of «one yavam to two yevamot,» as well as cases of two yevamin to one yevama. The Gemara comments: «Granted, according to» the opinion of «Rabbi Yoḥanan, who said» that once a yavam has performed ḥalitza with his yevama, «the entire household,» the woman who performed ḥalitza as well as her rival wives, «is liable due to a prohibition» derived from the verse “So shall it be done to the man who does not build his brother’s house” (Deuteronomy 25:9), but the women are not liable to karet due to the prohibition with regard to a brother’s wife. In light of Rabbi Yoḥanan’s ruling, «it was necessary to teach us that betrothal does not take effect on» the rival wife of the woman who performed ḥalitza, despite the fact that she is only «liable for» violating «a prohibition,» in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Akiva.
